Md. Ashfaqul Islam J. This civil appeal by leave at the instructed of the defendants appellants, is directed against the judgment and order dated 05.01.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1201 of 2008 making the Rule absolute by setting aside the judgment and decree dated 14.01.2008 passed by the learned Joint Division Judge, Patiya, Chittagong in order Appeal No. 269 of 2007 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the Judgment and decree dated 08.06.2004 by the Senior Assistant Judge, Banshkhali, Chitttagong in Other Suit No. 248 of 1997 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The trial court decreed the suit. The defendants preferred Other Appeal No. 269 of 2004 which was allowed by setting aside the judgment and decree of the trig court.

Mr. Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Advocate for the appellants contends that since the plaintiffs-respondents having admitted of their living in the suit property as in permissive possession, the High Court Division was wrong in making the Rule absolute decreeing the suit in holding that the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land had been uninterrupted and continuous to the knowledge of all including the defendants for more than 12 years. This has conferred upon the plaintiffs a good tile by adverse possession in addition to their title in the suit land otherwise acquired. Further, we have found that the High Court Division did not clarify the issue in that the plaintiffs claimed only 37 decimals of land out of 1 kani 14 gonda of land of the disputed kabala but the trial court decreed the suit on the entire quantum of land in favour of the plaintiffs which was beyond the prayer of the plaintiffs.
